quarterly_data.signal: The earnings release Statistics table (GWh; its footnote says it includes the proportionate share of output where Constellation has an undivided ownership interest in jointly-owned generating plants) shows total nuclear generation of 44,160 GWh for the three months ended June 30, 2026 versus 45,170 GWh a year earlier, natural gas, oil and renewables generation of 30,649 GWh versus 5,560 GWh, and total supply of 89,815 GWh versus 65,641 GWh.
quarterly_data.figure: three months ended June 30, 2026 vs 2025: nuclear generation 44,160 GWh vs 45,170 GWh; natural gas, oil and renewables 30,649 GWh vs 5,560 GWh; total supply 89,815 GWh vs 65,641 GWh

quarterly_data.signal: The earnings presentation's 2028/2029 PJM Capacity Auction Results slide shows Constellation's cleared volumes (rounded, at ownership, excluding generation assets held for sale) totalling 18,875 MW for its PJM portfolio, 15,700 MW nuclear and 3,175 MW fossil/others, at a price of $325 per MW-day in each zone listed (RTO, ComEd, EMAAC, MAAC, BGE).
quarterly_data.figure: 2028/2029 PJM auction: 18,875 MW cleared (15,700 MW nuclear, 3,175 MW fossil/others) at $325/MW-day

quarterly_data.signal: The earnings presentation says its growth outlook excludes potential upside from capturing premium value for 147 million MWhs of annual and available nuclear generation in 2029 and from securing additional natural gas contracts. Its detailed base-earnings modeling inputs list contracted clean volumes of 36, 45, 53, 54 and 53 million MWhs for 2026 through 2030; the footnote says contracted clean volumes are updated annually and do not include PPAs signed in 2026.
